title: Storage and Data Movement
summary: Analyze how storage and network movement affect compute workloads.
objectives: Compare storage capacity, throughput, latency, and durability concepts.
Trace storage to network to compute relationships.

vocab.def: The time required for a response or transfer to begin or complete.
The amount of data moved or work completed over time.
The ability of stored data to remain available over time.

sections.heading: Data movement matters
sections.body: A fast compute resource may wait when storage or network movement is constrained. Consider the relationship storage -> network -> compute instead of looking only at processor utilization.

sections.heading: Storage choices have tradeoffs
sections.body: Local, shared, block, object, and file storage represent different access and management concepts. Capacity, performance, latency, durability, and redundancy remain contextual.

practice.prompt: GPU utilization is low while storage throughput is below the workload requirement. What is a plausible explanation?
practice.answer: The compute resource may be waiting for data; storage or the path to it may be a bottleneck.

quiz.question: What can limit a powerful compute workload?
options: A constrained storage or network data path
quiz.answer: A constrained storage or network data path

lab.objective: Trace synthetic data movement and identify a constrained link.

futureCompetencyCandidates: reason about storage and data movement constraints
